_comment: Filter chain ORDER (filter-effects-1 §2: 'The filter functions are applied in the order provided' — the output of each is the input to the next, left to right). Base colour #3498db = (52,152,219) on a 120x40 box. The repo's measured grayscale basis is Rec.709 weights on gamma-encoded sRGB (fixtures/properties/effects/filter-grayscale-basis.json: 54/182/18): gray(c) = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B. sepia(1) matrix (filter-effects-1 §8.5): R'=.393R+.769G+.189B; G'=.349R+.686G+.168B; B'=.272R+.534G+.131B. ARITHMETIC — gray(52,152,219) = 11.055+108.710+15.812 = 135.58 -> (135.58,135.58,135.58). CASE A 'grayscale(1) sepia(1)' (gray first): sepia on the grey: R'=135.58*(.393+.769+.189)=135.58*1.351=183.2; G'=135.58*1.203=163.1; B'=135.58*0.937=127.0 -> (183,163,127); with 8-bit inter-stage quantisation (gray->136): (183.7,163.6,127.4) -> at most 1 off, inside tolerance. CASE B 'sepia(1) grayscale(1)' (sepia first): sepia(52,152,219) = (178.7,159.2,124.0) (the value STATUS pins for sepia 100%); gray of that = 0.2126*178.7+0.7152*159.2+0.0722*124.0 = 38.00+113.87+8.95 = 160.8 -> (161,161,161). The two orders differ by (22,2,-34) — far beyond tolerance 2 — and each single-stage control equals what a stage-dropping runtime would produce: apply-first-only gives (136,136,136)/(179,159,124), apply-last-only gives (179,159,124)/(136,136,136), all distinct from both correct answers by >=3 in some channel. box asserted only on the non-grey fills: the two grey results ((161,161,161) and (136,136,136)) sit on the greyscale axis where harness-label antialiasing pixels could pollute a bbox, so those assert fill only. No predicted red — this closes the order hole that no fixture exercised; sepia itself was fixed on iOS 2026-08-28 and stays pinned by filter-sepia-amounts.json.
